description: International Rectifier / Infineon HEXFET fifth-generation planar N-channel power MOSFET, 200 V / 18 A / 0.15 ohm. Datasheet PD-95046A dated 07/23/10, 11 pages, covers THREE package variants under one document: IRF640NPbF (TO-220AB), IRF640NSPbF (D2Pak = TO-263AB) and IRF640NLPbF (TO-262). The ordered part IRF640NSTRLPBF is the D2Pak, tape-and-reel order code; the datasheet's own part name for that variant is IRF640NSPbF. IMPORTANT: because the document is shared, several parameters are footnoted to a specific package - see layout_notes for which thermal numbers apply to D2Pak and which are TO-220AB only. This datasheet contains NO application/layout section, NO decoupling guidance, and NO recommended land pattern (it defers the footprint to IR application note AN-994, which is not part of the PDF). It also never maps the package lead numbers 1/2/3 to Gate/Drain/Source - see OPEN and the per-pin notes.

pinout.name: G
pinout.notes: GATE. ASSIGNMENT IS NOT FROM THE LCSC-HOSTED PDF - see layout_notes entry 'PIN ASSIGNMENT PROVENANCE' for the full citation list. The D2Pak (TO-263AB) outline on p.9 of PD-95046A numbers the three gull-wing leads 1, 2, 3 (left to right in the pin-down front view) but never maps them to G/D/S; the only G/D/S labels in the 11-page PDF are on the schematic symbol (p.1, p.2), which carries no pin numbers. Established externally: (a) Nexperia D2PAK (SOT404, JEDEC TO-263AB) 'Pinning information' table gives pin 1 = G = gate; (b) the Vishay IRF640S / SiHF640S datasheet - the same device type in the same TO-263AB outline - labels the LEFT lead of the D2PAK 'G' in its device-orientation figure, and its TO-263AB package drawing numbers that same left lead '1'; (c) Infineon's own board-assembly note states the TO transistor lead order as 'gate, drain, source'. KiCad cross-check: the pulled easyeda2kicad symbol names pin 1 'G' - AGREES.

pinout.name: D
pinout.notes: DRAIN - and electrically the SAME NODE as the tab. ASSIGNMENT IS NOT FROM THE LCSC-HOSTED PDF - see layout_notes 'PIN ASSIGNMENT PROVENANCE'. Centre lead. In the p.9 front view this lead alone is drawn TRUNCATED (it terminates at the body with no formed foot) and the lead callouts read '2x b' / '2x b2', i.e. only two of the three leads carry formed-lead metal dimensions - so geometrically lead 2 is a stub of the same stamping as the tab. Nexperia's D2PAK pinning table states exactly this for the JEDEC TO-263AB package: pin 2 = D = drain, footnote 'It is not possible to make connection to pin 2', and the package is described as '3 terminals (one lead cropped)'. WIRING WARNING: there is NO solderable land for pin 2. The drain must be taken from the tab. The pulled KiCad footprint has NO pad 2 at all and the pulled symbol has NO pin 2 - the drain terminal is numbered 4 in both. A netlist generator MUST wire the drain to symbol pin 4, never to '2' or 'TAB'.

pinout.name: S
pinout.notes: SOURCE. ASSIGNMENT IS NOT FROM THE LCSC-HOSTED PDF - see layout_notes 'PIN ASSIGNMENT PROVENANCE'. Third gull-wing lead, formed foot, carries the b/b2/L dimensions. Established externally: Nexperia D2PAK (SOT404 / TO-263AB) pinning table pin 3 = S = source; Vishay IRF640S device-orientation figure labels the RIGHT lead of the D2PAK 'S', and the Vishay TO-263AB drawing numbers that lead '3'. KiCad cross-check: the pulled symbol names pin 3 'S' - AGREES.

pinout.name: D_TAB
pinout.notes: DRAIN. The tab is electrically the DRAIN - established, not assumed. ASSIGNMENT IS NOT FROM THE LCSC-HOSTED PDF - see layout_notes 'PIN ASSIGNMENT PROVENANCE'. PD-95046A calls this surface only a THERMAL PAD (outline note 4: 'THERMAL PAD CONTOUR OPTIONAL WITHIN DIMENSION E, L1, D1 & E1') and never states its node. Established externally: (a) Nexperia D2PAK (SOT404 / JEDEC TO-263AB) 'Pinning information' table, row 'mb': symbol D, description 'mounting base; connected to drain'; (b) International Rectifier AN-994 - the very application note this datasheet defers to - Table 1 note 1: 'The Rth (JL) & the Rth (JA) 1sq" were measured at the same time. Rth reference to drain lead', with the body text identifying D2-Pak as one of the 'larger packages with exposed heat sinks', i.e. IR's own documentation treats the D2-Pak exposed heatsink/thermal terminal as the DRAIN; (c) the Vishay IRF640S device-orientation figure puts 'D' on the cropped centre lead, which is one stamping with the tab. Same node as pin 2. BOARD-LEVEL CONSEQUENCE for LUM-DTR-STROBE-A: the tab is in the 48 V drain domain, so this ~8.4 x 10.6 mm land plus its drain pour is LIVE HIGH-VOLTAGE COPPER - clearance/creepage must be enforced against it - and it is thermally the only path out of the die (RthJC 1.0 C/W). KiCad cross-check: the pulled footprint's tab land is pad 4 and the pulled symbol names pin 4 'D' - AGREES electrically; only the NUMBER differs (4, not 'TAB').

land_pattern.package: D2Pak / TO-263AB (p.9 outline note 8: 'OUTLINE CONFORMS TO JEDEC OUTLINE TO-263AB')
land_pattern.notes: NOT A RECOMMENDED LAND PATTERN - this datasheet does not publish one. p.11 note: 'This is applied to D2Pak, when mounted on 1" square PCB (FR-4 or G-10 Material). For recommended footprint and soldering techniques refer to application note #AN-994.' AN-994 is NOT included in this PDF. Everything below is read off the p.9 D2Pak PACKAGE OUTLINE table, i.e. body/lead geometry, not solder-land geometry; treat fp_verify results accordingly. pitch_mm = e = 2.54 BSC (lead pitch, 0.100 in BSC). pad_count = 4 counts the three gull-wing leads (1,2,3) plus the single exposed thermal tab; a KiCad TO-263 footprint that merges the tab land into a lead land (e.g. TabPin2 variants) may report a different copper-pad count - reconcile that before trusting a pad_count error. pad_size_mm DELIBERATELY OMITTED: the PDF gives lead metal widths only, never land sizes. PACKAGE OUTLINE TABLE (mm, min/max): A 4.06/4.83; A1 0.00/0.254; b 0.51/0.99; b1 0.51/0.89; b2 1.14/1.78; b3 1.14/1.73; c 0.38/0.74; c1 0.38/0.58; c2 1.14/1.65; D (body length) 8.38/9.65; D1 6.86/-; E (body width) 9.65/10.67; E1 6.22/-; e 2.54 BSC; H (overall height incl. formed leads) 14.61/15.88; L 1.78/2.79; L1 -/1.65; L2 -/1.78; L3 0.25 BSC; L4 4.78/5.28. OUTLINE NOTES: (3) D & E do not include mold flash; flash shall not exceed 0.127 mm (.005 in) per side, measured at the outermost extremes of the plastic body at datum plane H. (4) Thermal pad contour optional within dimension E, L1, D1 & E1. (5) Dimension b1 and c1 apply to base metal only. (6) Datum A & B to be determined at datum plane H. (7) Controlling dimension: inch. (8) Outline conforms to JEDEC outline TO-263AB.

layout_notes: SOA (Fig 8, p.4) - THE PUBLISHED PULSE-WIDTH LINES ARE 10us, 100us, 1ms AND 10ms ONLY. There is NO DC line, and the plot does NOT extend to 100 ms or 200 ms. The legend box reads exactly 'TC = 25 C / TJ = 175 C / Single Pulse' - the SOA is referenced to CASE temperature 25 C, not ambient.

SOA drain current at Vds = 10 V, taken from the Fig 8 vector geometry (axis calibration cross-checked: the +1-slope left boundary is exactly the Rds(on) = 0.15 ohm line, and the top plateau is exactly Idm = 72 A): 10us -> 72 A (still clamped by the 72 A Idm plateau); 100us -> 72 A (plateau); 1ms -> 53 A; 10ms -> 20 A. The sloped branch of each line is a constant-power line of 8200 W (10us), 2001 W (100us), 534 W (1ms), 200 W (10ms); each line ends at the Vdss = 200 V dashed boundary at 41 A / 10 A / 2.7 A / 1.0 A respectively.

THE BOARD'S 5-200 ms LINEAR-MODE PULSES ARE OFF THE PUBLISHED SOA AND MUST BE DERIVED. Grounded basis for a derivation, entirely from this PDF: all four Fig 8 constant-power lines satisfy P * Zth(j-c)(t) = 150 C exactly against the Fig 11 single-pulse curve (8200 x 0.0183 = 150; 2001 x 0.0751 = 150; 534 x 0.280 = 150; 200 x 0.749 = 150). This SOA is therefore a PURE THERMAL (Zth) LIMIT - the plot shows no secondary-breakdown / Spirito derating knee anywhere. Extending the same rule gives ~151 W at 100 ms and ~150 W at 200 ms, which lands on the Pd = 150 W @ Tc = 25 C rating. CAVEAT: whether a planar HEXFET is actually thermally stable in linear mode at those pulse widths is NOT answered by this datasheet - see the Fig 3 crossover note.

Fig 11 (p.5) MAXIMUM EFFECTIVE TRANSIENT THERMAL IMPEDANCE, JUNCTION-TO-CASE, SINGLE PULSE, normalized (multiply by RthJC = 1.0 C/W max): t = 10us -> 0.018; 100us -> 0.075; 1ms -> 0.280; 5ms -> 0.59; 10ms -> 0.749; 25ms -> 0.92; 50ms -> 0.97; 100ms -> 0.99; >=150ms -> 1.00 (fully steady state). Beyond ~150 ms the device is at DC and the limit is the 150 W Pd @ Tc = 25 C with 1.0 W/C linear derating. Fig 11 notes: duty factor D = t1/t2; peak Tj = P_DM x Zth(jc) + Tc.

THERMAL RESISTANCE (p.2), with the footnotes that decide which package each applies to: RthJC junction-to-case 1.0 C/W MAX (no typ). RthCS case-to-sink, flat greased surface 0.50 C/W typ - footnoted 'This is only applied to TO-220AB package'. RthJA junction-to-ambient 62 C/W max - same TO-220AB-only footnote. RthJA junction-to-ambient (PCB mount) 40 C/W max - footnoted 'This is applied to D2Pak, when mounted on 1" square PCB (FR-4 or G-10 Material)'. So the ONLY D2Pak RthJA figure in this datasheet, 40 C/W, ASSUMES ONE SQUARE INCH (645 mm2) of FR-4/G-10 PCB copper. p.1 adds that the D2Pak 'can dissipate up to 2.0W in a typical surface mount application'.

Vgs(th) GATE THRESHOLD VOLTAGE: 2.0 V MIN, 4.0 V MAX, no typ published; conditions Vds = Vgs, Id = 250 uA. The 2.0 V spread between min and max is the matching problem for five paralleled/independent linear stages.

TRANSFER CHARACTERISTIC / TEMPERATURE COEFFICIENT (Fig 3, p.3; conditions Vds = 50 V, 20 us pulse width). The Tj = 25 C and Tj = 175 C curves CROSS at approximately Vgs = 6.4 V, Id = 24 A (zero-temperature-coefficient point). BELOW ~24 A the Tj = 175 C curve lies ABOVE the Tj = 25 C curve, i.e. POSITIVE current temperature coefficient - the thermally unstable / current-hogging region. The board's ~2.6 A pass current is deep inside that positive-tempco region. Curve sample points (Vgs -> Id at Tj=25 C / Id at Tj=175 C): 4.50 -> 0.71 A / 3.73 A; 4.86 -> 2.4 / 6.5; 5.22 -> 5.8 / 10.1; 5.59 -> 10.7 / 14.2; 5.95 -> 16.6 / 18.7; 6.31 -> 23.1 / 23.3; 6.66 -> 29.9 / 28.2; 7.03 -> 36.5 / 33.1; 8.11 -> 56.7 / 48.3; 9.00 -> 72.0 / 56.7. No numeric temperature coefficient of Vgs(th) or of Id is tabulated anywhere; only the breakdown voltage tempco is given (0.25 V/C typ, ref 25 C, Id = 1 mA).

GATE DRIVE LOAD (the op-amp drives this gate directly): Qg 67 nC MAX, Qgs 11 nC max, Qgd (Miller) 33 nC max, all at Id = 11 A, Vds = 160 V, Vgs = 10 V. Ciss 1160 pF typ, Coss 185 pF typ, Crss 53 pF typ at Vgs = 0 V, Vds = 25 V, f = 1.0 MHz. Fig 5 (p.4) shows Ciss RISING to roughly 2000 pF as Vds falls toward 1 V - the low-Vds end of a linear-mode drop is the high-capacitance end. Switching times (Vdd = 100 V, Id = 11 A, Rg = 2.5 ohm, Rd = 9.0 ohm): td(on) 10 ns, tr 19 ns, td(off) 23 ns, tf 5.5 ns typ. Internal package inductance: Ld 4.5 nH, Ls 7.5 nH (between lead 6 mm / 0.25 in from package and centre of die contact).

Rds(on) 0.15 ohm MAX at Vgs = 10 V, Id = 11 A (footnoted: pulse width <= 400 us, duty cycle <= 2%). Fig 4 (p.3) normalized Rds(on) vs Tj at Vgs = 10 V, Id = 18 A: about 0.5x at -60 C, 1.0x at 25 C, rising monotonically to about 2.9x at 175 C. Forward transconductance gfs 6.8 S MIN at Vds = 50 V, Id = 11 A.

BODY DIODE (source-drain): Is continuous 18 A, Ism pulsed 72 A; Vsd 1.3 V max at Tj = 25 C, Is = 11 A, Vgs = 0 V; trr 167 ns typ / 251 ns max; Qrr 929 nC typ / 1394 nC max at Tj = 25 C, If = 11 A, di/dt = 100 A/us. Peak diode recovery dv/dt 8.1 V/ns max (conditions: Isd <= 11 A, di/dt <= 344 A/us, Vdd <= V(BR)Dss, Tj <= 175 C).

AVALANCHE: Eas 247 mJ single pulse (conditions: starting Tj = 25 C, L = 4.2 mH, Rg = 25 ohm, Ias = 11 A); Iar 18 A; Ear 15 mJ repetitive (repetitive rating; pulse width limited by max junction temperature). Fig 12c (p.6) plots Eas vs starting Tj for Id = 4.4 A / 7.6 A / 11 A, falling from about 550 mJ at 25 C to zero at 175 C for the 4.4 A curve.

THE VENDOR PRINTS NO APPLICATION LAYOUT SECTION. The only 'Circuit Layout Considerations' in the document (p.7) belong to the peak-diode-recovery dv/dt TEST FIXTURE, not to an application: 'Low Stray Inductance', 'Ground Plane', 'Low Leakage Inductance Current Transformer'. There is no decoupling guidance, no Kelvin-source guidance, no copper-area recommendation beyond the 1 in-square RthJA condition, and no keepout guidance anywhere in this PDF.

FOOTPRINT/ASSEMBLY: recommended footprint and soldering technique are explicitly deferred to Infineon/IR application note AN-994 (p.11 note), which is not in this PDF. Soldering temperature 300 C for 10 seconds, 1.6 mm from case. Mounting torque 10 lbf-in (1.1 N-m) for a 6-32 or M3 screw is footnoted TO-220AB-only and is irrelevant to the D2Pak. D2Pak tape & reel data is on p.11 (TRR and TRL feed directions, 330.00 mm max reel).

PIN ASSIGNMENT PROVENANCE - THE ASSIGNMENT IN 'pinout' DOES NOT COME FROM THE LCSC-HOSTED PDF (parts/C23708.pdf, PD-95046A 07/23/10). That document never maps lead numbers 1/2/3 to Gate/Drain/Source and never states the tab's electrical node; the pinout above was established from external primary sources on 2026-07-28 and is cited here in full because the primary PDF was silent. SOURCE 1 (package-level, explicit and numbered): Nexperia PSMN3R7-100BSE product data sheet, 3 September 2018, section 5 'Pinning information', Table 2, https://assets.nexperia.com/documents/data-sheet/PSMN3R7-100BSE.pdf - package 'D2PAK (SOT404)', Table 3 describing it as 'plastic, single-ended surface-mounted package (D2PAK); 3 terminals (one lead cropped); 2.54 mm pitch'. Table 2 reads: pin 1 / G / gate; pin 2 / D / drain [1]; pin 3 / S / source; mb / D / 'mounting base; connected to drain'; footnote [1] = 'It is not possible to make connection to pin 2.' SOURCE 2 (same device type, same JEDEC outline): Vishay Siliconix 'IRF640S, SiHF640S, SiHF640L Power MOSFET', document number 91037, rev. E 18-Jan-16, https://www.vishay.com/docs/91037/sihf640s.pdf - page 1 device-orientation figure labels the D2PAK (TO-263) leads G (left), D (centre, the cropped lead), S (right); the Vishay 'Package Information TO-263AB (HIGH VOLTAGE)' drawing bound into the same PDF (document number 91364, rev. 15-Sep-08) numbers those same three leads 1, 2, 3 left-to-right in the pin-down front view and carries note 7 'Outline conforms to JEDEC outline to TO-263AB', with a dimension table identical to PD-95046A p.9 (A 4.06/4.83, b 0.51/0.99, b2 1.14/1.78, D 8.38/9.65, E 9.65/10.67, e 2.54 BSC, H 14.61/15.88, L 1.78/2.79, L4 4.78/5.28) - i.e. it is the same drawing, so G/D/S maps onto leads 1/2/3. SOURCE 3 (tab = drain, from the original manufacturer): International Rectifier Application Note AN-994 'Maximizing the Effectiveness of Your SMD Assemblies', https://www.newark.com/pdfs/techarticles/ir/AppNote_AN-994.pdf - p.3 Table 1 note 1: 'The Rth (JL) & the Rth (JA) 1sq" were measured at the same time. Rth reference to drain lead', alongside body text calling D2-Pak one of the 'larger packages with exposed heat sinks (D2-Pak, D-Pak & SOT-223)'. SOURCE 4 (lead order, from Infineon): 'Recommendations for board assembly of Infineon transistor outline type packages', Revision 4.0, 2021-10-11, https://www.infineon.com/dgdl/Infineon-Recommendations_for_Board_Assembly_TO-P-v03_00-EN.pdf?fileId=5546d462580663ef0158069840880338 - section 1.1 covers PG-TO263 (D2PAK); section 4.1 'Lead bending' states 'The original straight alignment of the leads (gate, drain, source of a transistor package) ...'. NEGATIVE FINDINGS worth not re-litigating: (i) the Infineon-hosted revision of this datasheet (Infineon-IRF640N-DataSheet-v01_01-EN.pdf, https://www.infineon.com/dgdl/Infineon-IRF640N-DataSheet-v01_01-EN.pdf?fileId=5546d462533600a4015355e7be9019ee) is the SAME PD-95046A 07/23/10 document and adds no pin labelling - the Infineon-hosted copy does NOT close this gap; (ii) AN-994, which p.11 of the datasheet names as the source of the 'recommended footprint', contains NO land pattern or footprint drawing of any kind (its 7 pages are Rth measurement method, thermal characterisation, attachment to board, solder pastes, reflow heat profiles, rework) - that footprint pointer is a dead end; (iii) JEDEC TO-263AB is a mechanical outline registration only - neither IR's nor Vishay's TO-263AB drawing, both of which declare JEDEC conformance, assigns lead functions.

KICAD LIBRARY CROSS-CHECK (lib_pull --lcsc C23708 --verify-load, 2026-07-28, load_check ok). SYMBOL 'IRF640NSTRLPBF' in lib/aiee.kicad_sym: pin 1 name 'G', pin 3 name 'S', pin 4 name 'D'. THERE IS NO PIN 2. FOOTPRINT 'aiee:TO-263-2_L10.0-W9.1-P5.08-LS15.2-TL' (legacy '(module ...)' format, which is normal for easyeda2kicad pulls and loads fine in KiCad 10): 3 COPPER PADS - pad 1 rect 4.000 x 1.300 mm at (-5.09, -2.54), pad 3 rect 4.000 x 1.300 mm at (-5.09, +2.54), pad 4 rect 8.400 x 10.566 mm at (+5.09, 0.00) = the tab land. Lead pads 1 and 3 are 5.08 mm apart (2 x the 2.54 mm nominal pitch) because the cropped centre lead has no land - hence the 'TO-263-2' (two-lead) name and the 'P5.08' in it. VERDICT - ELECTRICAL AGREEMENT: the pulled library agrees with all four external sources (gate on lead 1, source on lead 3, drain on the tab); there is NO electrical contradiction. NUMBERING MISMATCH (must be honoured by any generator): easyeda2kicad numbers the drain/tab terminal '4' and omits '2' entirely, whereas the datasheet/JEDEC numbering is leads 1/2/3 plus an unnumbered tab. So DRAIN MUST BE WIRED TO SYMBOL PIN 4 - wiring to '2' or to 'TAB' will not connect. PAD_COUNT RECONCILIATION: land_pattern.pad_count = 4 in this file counts the three package leads plus the tab (package reality); the pulled footprint exposes 3 copper pads. An fp_verify pad_count mismatch of 4 vs 3 on this part is EXPECTED and is NOT a real error - it is the D2PAK 'one lead cropped' construction, where pin 2 has no formed foot and therefore no solder land. This footprint is the merged-land variant (tab land carries the drain), not a 4-copper-pad variant.
